title: Sephiria Hard Mode Unlock: Finish Chapter 2 → Root’s Retreat
description: Unlock Sephiria Hard Mode (Root’s Retreat): finish Chapter 2, talk to the village tree, then clear Stage 1 / 15 / 30. Notes the outdated Destiny free-node path.
h1: Sephiria Hard Mode unlock: Chapter 2 → Root’s Retreat
meta: For sephiria roots retreat / hard mode / how to unlock hard mode.
body:
Players search sephiria roots retreat, sephiria hard mode, and how to unlock hard mode because Hard Mode is gated and still listed under the Root’s Retreat achievement names.

The gate has two halves: a story step and a conversation. Neither is a sapphire purchase. What the page cannot tell you is how many stages exist in total — the public record documents three clear milestones and no maximum.

Current unlock (post Update 0.7.55)

  1. Finish Chapter 2 (story progress, not just a random boss).
  2. Return to Bunnyville and talk to the Destiny tree.
  3. Open dialogue topics and select Hard Mode.

After that conversation, Hard Mode / Root’s Retreat becomes available for later runs. You do not need to buy a paid Destiny node on the normal path.

What each step in the chain gates

StepWhat it gatesHow you know it is doneWhat it does not prove
Finish Chapter 2The village tree will discuss Hard Mode at allStory progress past Chapter 2, not a single boss killThat the dialogue option has been taken
Talk to the tree in BunnyvilleAccess to the dialogue topicsThe conversation opens with topic choicesThat Hard Mode is selected — a menu can be opened and left
Select the Hard Mode topicRoot’s Retreat on later runsThe option is accepted in dialogueThat the entrance UI appears immediately; community threads report lag
Clear Stage 1The Root’s Retreat achievementStage 1 clearedAnything about Stage 15 or the total stage count
Clear Stage 15The Root’s Retreat 15 achievementStage 15 clearedA stage cap, a reward table or a difficulty ceiling
Clear Stage 30The Root’s Retreat 30 achievementStage 30 clearedThat the mode ends there

Built from the unlock steps and the achievement names already published on this page. The last column matters because achievement lists record what was cleared, not what the mode contains.

Root’s Retreat stages and achievements

Steam achievements treat Root’s Retreat as Hard Mode stage clears, not a separate village:

  • Root’s Retreat — clear Hard Mode Stage 1
  • Root’s Retreat 15 — clear Stage 15
  • Root’s Retreat 30 — clear Stage 30

Read the three names as a progression record rather than a content list. They confirm that Stage 1, 15 and 30 are clearable and that the mode keeps counting past the first clear; they say nothing about the numbers between them or about what follows 30.

Version trap: Steam “Basic Guide” and some EA discussions still say Hard Mode is a free node at the bottom of Destiny Inscription. That was true early on; TEAM HORAY moved the regular unlock to the tree dialogue in 0.7.55. If a guide only sends you to Destiny Inscription, treat it as legacy.

Why the free-node advice spread

The old instruction was accurate for the build it described. Early access placed the unlock at the bottom of the sapphire board, so walkthroughs written then sent readers to Destiny Inscription and told them to look for a free node there.

That produces a specific kind of stuck session: the player owns the story progress, stands at the board, and finds no such node. Nothing is broken. The unlock moved to a conversation, and the conversation is the thing to look for.

Preparing for Root’s Retreat Stage 15 and 30

Choose a build you can assemble consistently before increasing the stage difficulty. Use Wishing Fountain picks to prepare your starting Artifacts, then follow one weapon and Artifact family rather than spreading upgrades across unrelated tags. The Companion build is one community-reported option.

The achievement list documents clears at Stage 1, 15 and 30. Those milestones do not establish a maximum stage count or a complete reward table; check the current game for stage-specific modifiers.

Preparation checklist before Stage 1

  1. Settle the build. Pick a setup you can assemble consistently; a run that depends on one specific offer is not ready for a harder version of the dungeon.
  2. Commit to one weapon and one Artifact family before raising the stage, which is the same discipline the builds page applies to normal runs.
  3. Set the fountain picks so the opening Artifacts support that family, and confirm the capacity you actually have rather than the default.
  4. Re-read the Floor 3 boss notes. Erma, the Mad Scientist, occupies that slot, and from Chapter 2 onward Pantaxis can replace her, so the habit you learn may not be the fight you get — see Erma and the final boss section.
  5. Check the talent budget in-client after the unlock instead of planning around a total from a video, because the number moves between patches.

Legacy / failsafe notes

  • Very old saves may still see a Destiny Inscription fallback (Steam discussion era / later failsafe patches).
  • If the tree says Hard Mode unlocked but you cannot find the entrance UI, check Sapphire/Destiny menus and restart the hub—community threads report UI lag after unlock.

Those two notes explain most of the contradictory reports. A player on an old save can legitimately see the old path, and a player on a current save can legitimately see the new dialogue but a delayed interface.

What Hard Mode is for

Hard Mode adds tougher dungeon modifiers (community 1.0 writeups list many “elements” / challenge toggles) and is the place people take proven builds after clearing the story route. Talent budget also expands once Hard Mode access is online—exact talent totals can change by patch, so verify in-client.

Common mistakes and their causes

  • Standing at Destiny Inscription looking for a node. The cause is a legacy guide rather than a broken save. Chapter 2 plus the village tree conversation is the current path.
  • Treating Stage 30 as the end of the mode. Three achievement names record three clears. They do not state a maximum, so no plan should assume the mode stops at 30.
  • Reading the achievements as a reward list. They document clears, not drops. With no complete reward table in the public record, stage rewards have to be checked in the current game.
  • Climbing stages with a half-built run. A modifier that punishes a missing piece turns a working story build into a failed run; the fix is finishing the build, not retrying the stage.
  • Planning talents against an old number. The budget expands with access and the exact total is patch-bound.
  • Assuming the entrance failed to unlock. If the dialogue confirmed it and the UI is absent, community threads point at lag; check the Sapphire / Destiny menus and restart the hub before redoing Chapter 2.

What this page does not cover

  • Which build to carry into the stages, and why some routes need a specific Artifact before they function — see builds and the Companion route.
  • Weapon upgrade routes and the branch a run commits to — see weapons and upgrades.
  • The first-session order, Side Bag rules and early unlocks — see the beginner guide.
  • How the tree gates weapon training and talents before hard mode — see Destiny Inscription.
  • Co-op behaviour on harder runs, including party scaling and revives — see co-op play.
  • Where the Artifacts and Tablets you are carrying actually apply — see Artifacts and Tablets.

Quick FAQ

Do I need to buy a Destiny node for Hard Mode?

No. On the normal path the unlock is the village tree dialogue after Chapter 2. The paid-node version belongs to the early-access layout, so a guide that sends you to the sapphire board is describing a build that no longer matches the current tree.

When does Hard Mode become available — before or after the story ends?

After Chapter 2, not at the end of the story. That is why builds are expected to be assembled before Stage 1: the mode opens while there is still story route left to practise on.

Is Root’s Retreat a separate village?

No. The achievements treat it as Hard Mode stage clears, so it is the same dungeon under harder conditions rather than a new hub. Its documented milestones are Stage 1, 15 and 30.

How many stages are there?

The public record documents clears at Stage 1, 15 and 30 and states no maximum. Treat any larger figure you see quoted as unverified until the current game shows it.

Why is my talent budget different from a video’s?

Because the budget expands once Hard Mode access is online and the totals change between patches. Check the number in your client after the unlock instead of planning around a recorded one.

Should I start hard mode with the Companion build?

It is one community-reported option, not a requirement. What matters first is that you can assemble the setup consistently; the caveats on the build page apply here as well.

Related: Destiny Inscription · Builds · Final boss.

Before you push a higher stage, make sure you can keep your build together: Side Bag items stay inactive, so count your active inventory rather than what you have stored, and use secret-room cracks for extra supplies between runs.
